question.knowledge_point: Identifying Subsets of a Given Set
question.problem:
Which of the following sets is a subset of $A=\{3,6,9,12,15,18,21,…\}?$

I. $B=\{3n:n\in N,1\le n\le 4\}$

II. $C=\{6n:n\in N,1\le n\le 3\}$

III. $D=\{2n:n\in N,1\le n\le 4\}$
question.worked_solution:
First, we must find the elements of the sets $B,C$ and $D.$

- We find the elements of the set $B$ substituting the values $n\in \{1,2,3,4\}$ into the formula $3n,$ and we get the following elements:

$$
\begin{aligned}n=1 & \,⇒\,3(1)=3 \\ n=2 & \,⇒\,3(2)=6 \\ n=3 & \,⇒\,3(3)=9 \\ n=4 & \,⇒\,3(4)=12\end{aligned}
$$

So we have, $B=\{3,6,9,12\}.$

- On the other hand, the elements of the set $C$ can be found substituting the values $n\in \{1,2,3\}$ into the formula $6n,$ and we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}n=1 & \,⇒\,6(1)=6 \\ n=2 & \,⇒\,6(2)=12 \\ n=3 & \,⇒\,6(3)=18\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $C=\{6,12,18\}.$

- Finally, the elements of the set $D$ can be found substituting the values $n\in \{1,2,3,4\}$ into the formula $2n,$ and we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}n=1 & \,⇒\,2(1)=2 \\ n=2 & \,⇒\,2(2)=4 \\ n=3 & \,⇒\,2(3)=6 \\ n=4 & \,⇒\,2(4)=8\end{aligned}
$$

So we have, $D=\{2,4,6,8\}.$

Now, a set is a subset of $A$ if all of its elements are also elements of $A.$ With that in mind, let's inspect each option.

- $B=\{3,6,9,12\}$ is a subset of $A.\,✓$

- $C=\{6,12,18\}$ is a subset of $A.\,✓$

- $D=\{2,4,6,8\}$ is *not* a subset of $A$ because it contains the element $2\notin A.\,\times $

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only".
